summary: This Dockerfile builds a development container for Quarto documentation projects. It starts with a Quarto base image, installs system dependencies and optional tools (like spell-checking, pre-commit hooks, and Graphviz) in separate stages for efficiency, then creates a non-root user and configures bash with helpful aliases and welcome messages.

explanations.1: This line enables a newer Docker syntax feature that allows better caching of package manager operations.
explanations.3: This tells the spell-checker to ignore errors in this file, since it contains shell commands and paths that aren't real words.
explanations.4: We're starting from a pre-built image that already has Quarto installed, rather than installing it ourselves from scratch.
explanations.6: These ARG lines define variables that can be passed in when building the image, setting defaults like the username 'vscode' and user ID 1000.
explanations.24: The --mount flags create temporary caches during the build so apt package lists don't need to be re-downloaded if the build is repeated.
explanations.26: The 'set -eux' makes the shell script stricter: it fails on errors, shows commands as they run, and treats undefined variables as errors.
explanations.45: This allows the user to run sudo commands without entering a password, which is handy for development but wouldn't be done in production.
explanations.48: We're caching the yq download so if this step is repeated, we don't re-download it from the internet.
explanations.56: We're creating a new stage called 'extras' that builds on top of 'base', allowing us to skip installing optional tools if we don't need them.
explanations.65: This checks if a build argument is literally the string 'true', then runs the indented commands only if that condition is met.
explanations.78: We cache the npm package cache directory so repeated builds don't re-download Node packages.
explanations.83: We tell npm to use the cached directory we mounted instead of its default location, keeping the cache outside the container.
explanations.113: These lines use parameter expansion syntax (${VAR:-default}) to use the passed-in values or fall back to defaults if not provided.
explanations.116: We create a user group with the specified GID, then create a user account that belongs to that group.
explanations.127: This switches from running as root to running as the non-root user for all subsequent commands.
explanations.130: We cache Quarto's tools directory so if Chromium is already installed, we don't re-download it.
explanations.139: We're appending multiple lines to the user's .bashrc file to configure bash history and set up useful aliases.
explanations.151: The 'cat <<EOF' syntax is a heredoc, which lets us append a multi-line block of text into the file in one command.
